newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state considers options in AOL case.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state considers options in AOL case.

text.p: Washington State is considering a range of options as part of multistate negotiations aimed at resolving consumer complaints against America Online Inc , an official said Friday.

"Obviously one of the options is to file a lawsuit and obtain relief through the courts," said senior assistant attorney general Sally Gustafson. "Another option is to negotiate a settlement to a lawsuit and file both at the same time."
She said the state's Consumer Protection Act allows the state to seek court injunctions, civil penalties of up to $2,000 per infraction, consumer restitution and reimbursement of state costs.

She declined to comment on strategy being pursued by Washington and 19 other states in the talks with America Online, which stem from widespread complaints over an inability to gain access to the online service since it switched to a flat-rate billing system.
Other states involved in the multistate initiative include Illinois, Florida, Texas and New York, Gustafson said.
